name: Film and TV trivia (hard)
description: 43 hard questions about films, television, animation, actors, directors, from any decade. Written by Claude from cited web pages; every question names its page. Checked by a second model pass; the questions it flagged were corrected or left out.

source.name: Web pages cited on each question

items.question: For which category did Citizen Kane win its only Academy Award, despite nine nominations?
items.explain: Citizen Kane was nominated for nine Academy Awards but won only one, for original screenplay.

items.question: Which scene of Citizen Kane was the final one shot during production?
items.explain: The opening scene, in which the dying Kane whispers 'Rosebud', was shot in one take and was the last scene filmed.

source.title: 15 Facts About Orson Welles' CITIZEN KANE – AFI

items.question: In which year did Vertigo top the Sight and Sound critics' poll, ending Citizen Kane's long run in first place?
items.explain: Vertigo topped the 2012 poll and ended Kane's 50-year reign. It fell to second in 2022.

items.question: Vertigo received only two Academy Award nominations on its original release. Which categories were they?
items.explain: Despite its later reputation, Vertigo was nominated only for Art Direction and Sound.

source.title: Film Notes: VERTIGO – Yale University Library

items.question: According to one account, Hitchcock developed Vertigo's signature dolly-zoom technique from a drunken experience at which event?
items.explain: A Cambridge University Press piece says Hitchcock based the dolly-plus-zoom shot on a drunken experience at the Chelsea Arts Ball.

source.title: Vertigo: an overnight success in 54 years – Cambridge Core

items.question: Which prize did Kurosawa's Seven Samurai win at the 1954 Venice International Film Festival?
items.explain: Seven Samurai won the Silver Lion at Venice in 1954. The Golden Lion went to Kurosawa's Rashomon three years earlier.

items.question: What technical approach did Kurosawa innovate for the final battle of Seven Samurai?
answers: A multi-camera setup with telephoto lenses
Slow-motion photography at high frame rates
items.correct: A multi-camera setup with telephoto lenses
items.explain: Kurosawa used several cameras and telephoto lenses to shape how the audience perceived the battle.

items.question: Which composer scored Kurosawa's Rashomon, Ikiru and Seven Samurai?
items.explain: Hayasaka composed the music for these Kurosawa films, among others.

items.question: Which film won the Golden Lion at the 12th Venice International Film Festival in 1951?
items.explain: Kurosawa's Rashomon won the 1951 Golden Lion and drew Western attention to Japanese cinema.

items.question: Which actress played Audrey Horne in the original Twin Peaks?
items.explain: Sherilyn Fenn played Audrey Horne, the character created by Mark Frost and David Lynch.

items.question: How many nominations did Twin Peaks receive for its first season at the 42nd Primetime Emmy Awards?
items.explain: Twin Peaks earned fourteen Emmy nominations for its first season.

items.question: What is the title of the 1992 feature film that serves as a prequel to the Twin Peaks series?
items.explain: Twin Peaks: Fire Walk with Me (1992) is the prequel feature to the series.

items.question: Which stage actor, father of co-creator Mark Frost, was cast in the original Twin Peaks as a doctor?
items.explain: Warren Frost, Mark Frost's father, was cast as the town doctor.

items.question: Fritz Lang said his first sight of which city's skyline inspired Metropolis?
items.explain: Lang claimed he was inspired by his first glimpse of the New York skyline.

items.question: In 2008, a damaged print of Lang's original cut of Metropolis was found in a museum in which country?
items.explain: A 16 mm reduction negative of the original cut was found at the Museo del Cine in Buenos Aires.

items.question: Which actor played the inventor Rotwang in Fritz Lang's Metropolis?
items.explain: Rudolf Klein-Rogge played Rotwang. Alfred Abel played Joh Fredersen.

items.question: Who produced Metropolis at the Babelsberg Studio for UFA?
items.explain: Erich Pommer produced Metropolis at Babelsberg for Universum Film A.G. (UFA).

items.question: Who directed the pilot episode of The Wire, 'The Target'?
items.explain: Clark Johnson directed the series premiere, which aired on June 2, 2002.

items.question: Which former Baltimore homicide detective and schoolteacher worked with David Simon on The Corner and The Wire?
items.explain: Ed Burns, a former Baltimore police homicide detective and public school teacher, collaborated with Simon on both projects.

items.question: At which film festival was Spirited Away a co-recipient of the top prize in 2002?
items.explain: Spirited Away shared the Golden Bear at the 2002 Berlin International Film Festival.

items.question: Who produced Spirited Away for Studio Ghibli?
items.explain: Toshio Suzuki produced the film, which Miyazaki wrote and directed.

items.question: In Spirited Away, who is Yubaba's twin sister?
items.explain: Zeniba is Yubaba's twin sister. A shikigami that stowed away on Chihiro's back shapeshifts into her.

items.question: Which Miyazaki film was the first animated film to win the Japan Academy Film Prize for Picture of the Year?
items.explain: Princess Mononoke (1997) was the first animated film to win the prize.

source.title: List of works by Hayao Miyazaki – Wikipedia

items.question: Who wrote the 1959 novel on which Hitchcock's Psycho was based?
items.explain: Psycho (1960) was adapted from Robert Bloch's 1959 novel.

items.question: Who served as the body double for Janet Leigh in some shots of Psycho's shower scene?
items.explain: Marli Renfro was Leigh's body double in the shower scene.

items.question: Roughly what was the production budget of Psycho (1960)?
items.explain: Psycho had a budget of US$806,947 and earned about $50 million worldwide.

items.question: Whom did producer Hal Wallis want to direct Casablanca before Michael Curtiz got the job?
items.explain: Wallis's first choice was William Wyler, who became unavailable, so he chose Curtiz.

items.question: Casablanca was based on which unproduced stage play?
items.explain: The film was based on Murray Burnett and Joan Alison's unproduced play Everybody Comes to Rick's.

items.question: Which Australian writer scripted the first Doctor Who serial, An Unearthly Child?
items.explain: Anthony Coburn wrote An Unearthly Child, which introduced William Hartnell as the First Doctor.

items.question: Which event led the BBC to repeat the first episode of Doctor Who the following week?
answers: A technicians' strike at the BBC
items.explain: News of the Kennedy assassination overshadowed the first episode, so it was repeated before episode 2.

items.question: As of the mid-2020s, how many of William Hartnell's 134 episodes as a regular were missing from the archives?
items.explain: 42 of Hartnell's 134 episodes as a regular were missing in the mid-2020s. The number has changed before, when lost episodes turned up.

items.question: What was the concept of regeneration in Doctor Who initially called when it was introduced?
items.explain: It was first called a 'renewal' when Hartnell left because of his bad health.

items.question: In which century is the Doctor Who serial The Dalek Invasion of Earth set?
items.explain: In the serial, the Doctor and companions find Earth in the 22nd century occupied by Daleks.

source.title: The Dalek Invasion of Earth – Wikipedia

items.question: Which film's record of nine Academy Awards did Ben-Hur break at the 32nd Academy Awards?
items.explain: Ben-Hur won 11 Academy Awards, breaking the record of nine set the previous year by Gigi.

items.question: For the chariot race in Ben-Hur (1959), about how much sand was imported?
items.explain: Britannica notes that 40,000 tons of sand was imported for the chariot race, along with 300 sets and 8,000 extras.

items.question: Who won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor for Ben-Hur at the 32nd Academy Awards?
items.explain: Hugh Griffith won for playing Sheik Ilderim in Ben-Hur.

items.question: Which actress provided the voice of Snow White in Disney's 1937 film?
items.explain: Adriana Caselotti voiced Snow White in Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs.

source.title: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs (1937 film) – Wikipedia

items.question: What nickname did industry figures give Disney's risky first feature, Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs?
items.explain: A feature-length animated film was seen as such a gamble that industry figures dubbed it 'Disney's Folly'.

items.question: Who appeared at the 1973 Academy Awards to explain why Marlon Brando would not accept his Best Actor award for The Godfather?
items.explain: Brando boycotted the ceremony and sent Sacheen Littlefeather to explain why he could not collect the award.

items.question: For which film did Charlie Chaplin win his only competitive Academy Award, at the 1973 ceremony?
items.explain: Chaplin won Best Original Dramatic Score for Limelight, which became eligible because it did not screen in Los Angeles until 1972.

items.question: Which actor did Paramount reportedly want for Vito Corleone instead of Marlon Brando?
items.explain: Paramount preferred Ernest Borgnine and resisted Brando because he had delayed production on recent films.

items.question: David Chase directed only two episodes of The Sopranos: the pilot and which other episode?
items.explain: Chase directed the pilot and the series finale, 'Made in America'.

items.question: Which actor played Tony Blundetto in the fifth-season premiere of The Sopranos, 'Two Tonys'?
items.explain: Steve Buscemi played Tony Blundetto, Tony Soprano's cousin, in the season 5 opener.
